messages:

Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@biolens.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Initial MAP + sequencing question for MSA/DPA/order form

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency numbers and the deterministic billing examples. Procurement and legal want a clear mutual action plan (MAP) so we can align internal signoffs. A few clarifying asks from our side: 

- Can you outline the minimal gating order for legal artifacts (MSA vs DPA) relative to the order form signature? Our legal wants to know whether DPA needs to be signed before onboarding begins.
- For our pilot acceptance testing, we need explicit pass/fail criteria and an estimate of how long your legal/contracting team will take to review a redline.
- Please include any technical prerequisites (VPC endpoints, KMS integration checklist) that would block a pilot cutover schedule.

I attached a skeleton MAP (Biolens_MAP_v1.xlsx) — please populate and return so procurement can slot it into our internal project plan.

Regards,
Sara Lewis
Sr. Procurement Manager
Biolens Therapeutics
[Attachment: Biolens_MAP_v1.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@biolens.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@biolens.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial MAP + sequencing question for MSA/DPA/order form

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. I filled the MAP with a proposed sequence and attached (Biolens_MAP_v1.xlsx, updated). High level notes: 

1) Sequencing recommendation (order of sign-off to unblock pilot):
   - Step 0: Technical kickoff & prerequisites confirmed (network, KMS, test data access)
   - Step 1: DPA execution (we can run on our standard DPA; signature from both sides before pilot data is ingested)
   - Step 2: Order form (signed PO or order form) — this can be executed concurrently with the DPA if procurement needs order-of-record for billing, but we do not start pilot until DPA is signed
   - Step 3: MSA finalization and signature (MSA can be redlined in parallel with Step 1/2; MSA must be agreed before production rollout)

2) Legal turnaround expectations:
   - We typically provide initial redline within 3 business days for small edits, 7–10 business days for substantive changes. Marissa is copied to confirm.

3) Acceptance gating for pilot:
   - Delivery: Redwood will host a 2-week pilot environment with defined traffic patterns.
   - Criteria: 95th percentile latency <= 450ms for 90% of requests; successful KV-cache warming and repeatability checks; documented integration with Customer KMS for key wrapping.
   - Sign-off: Biolens engineering + procurement acceptance form (attached: Acceptance_Criteria_PO.pdf)

I've included Marissa for legal sequencing and Jonas for commercial timing. If this sequencing works we'll align dates and milestone owners in the MAP.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Sales, Mid-Market
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Biolens_MAP_v1.xlsx (updated)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@biolens.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 14:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial MAP + sequencing question for MSA/DPA/order form

Hi all — quick legal note on sequencing and practical redline expectations: 

- DPA before data ingress: strong preference. We can provision pilot accounts with synthetic data for earlier technical work, but any customer data ingestion should wait until the DPA is executed.
- MSA redlines: please share your preferred MSA sections you intend to redline (liability, indemnity, data residency, termination). For a single-cycle redline review we target 5 business days; for multi-issue reviews assume iterative cadence (~10–14 business days).
- Stand-up clause: we can agree on an interim ordering mechanism (signed order form with an explicit pilot scope and data constraints) that contains a clause tying production activation to execution of the MSA. That allows procurement to book spend while legal finalizes terms.

I attached a redline-ready MSA (MSA_draft_v3_redline.pdf) — Sara, if you can mark priority sections we will fast-track.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MSA_draft_v3_redline.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@biolens.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 11:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial MAP + sequencing question for MSA/DPA/order form

Sara — quick commercial note on sequencing that procurement often asks about: if you sign an order form to reserve pilot capacity we can guarantee the pilot window for a 30-day hold. For pilots with performance-sensitive workloads we recommend a staged acceptance:

- Week 0–1: Integration + smoke tests (no customer data)
- Week 2: Pilot with synthetic + limited production-like traffic (DPA must be signed to use any customer data)
- Week 3–4: Acceptance testing with production currents (post-DPA), formal sign-off and invoicing per order form terms

If Biolens needs a quick internal approval path, we can add a procurement-friendly line item into the order form for a non-recurring pilot fee and include a rollback/fallthrough clause tied to MSA signature. Ping me with the exact PO cadence and I’ll adapt the order form template.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
